description: A serene minimalist bedroom with an airy, Japandi-influenced aesthetic. The wall is finished in a textured off-white plaster with a subtly organic, uneven surface that adds quiet depth without pattern. A low-profile bed frame in warm walnut with a woven cane headboard insert dominates the lower frame, dressed in layers of soft linen bedding in cream and warm white with gentle wrinkles suggesting relaxed ease. To the right, a compact walnut nightstand holds a small ceramic vase with dried pampas grass and dried botanicals alongside a vintage-style brass alarm clock. A warm gentle glow emanates from just above and beside the headboard, softly illuminating the plaster wall and casting a narrow cone of warm light downward toward the nightstand surface. On the far right edge, sheer linen curtain panels in natural white diffuse soft daylight from an unseen window, adding a bright airy quality to the right side of the frame. The overall atmosphere is serene, restful, and organic, the palette restricted to off-whites, warm stone, natural walnut, and sandy beige. Camera at approximately standing eye-level, 5–6 feet high, using a normal lens and an off-center composition weighted toward the left — the bed and headboard fill the lower-left, the nightstand anchors the lower-right, and the warm wall glow draws the eye to the center-left. The entire composition is wide enough to establish the room corner context clearly.
